reason: S1 introduces supported_by_runtime_system() as the runtime-safety predicate for an implementation, and minify explicitly checks it before selecting an implementation. H0 instead invokes every member of simdjson::available_implementations without this check. On a host lacking an implementation's required_instruction_sets(), the harness can execute an unsupported backend rather than exercising a valid API state, potentially producing illegal-instruction crashes and misleading differential failures. H0 also does not directly validate the new predicate against the selection behavior represented by detect_best_supported().
evidence: implementation::supported_by_runtime_system() obtains required_instruction_sets() and detect_supported_architectures(), then requires `(supported_instruction_sets & required_instruction_sets) == required_instruction_sets`.
The changed minify main filters displayed implementations with `impl->supported_by_runtime_system()` and rejects a requested architecture when that predicate is false.

fuzz_implementations.cpp iterates all `simdjson::available_implementations`, assigns each to `simdjson::active_implementation`, and calls `e.parser.parse(Data,Size)` without checking `supported_by_runtime_system()`.
fuzz_minifyimpl.cpp calls `impl->minify(Data,Size,...)` for every available implementation without checking runtime support.
fuzz_utf8.cpp calls `impl->validate_utf8(...)` for every available implementation without checking runtime support.
recommended_action: Gate backend execution in all three harnesses with `supported_by_runtime_system()`, require at least one supported implementation, and compare only supported backends. Add a focused invariant check that `detect_best_supported()` returns a non-null runtime-supported implementation when any supported implementation exists.
